To what extent can a president weaken a federal organization?

The president appoints the director of the Office of Personnel Management which manages background investigations, writes the paychecks (as authorized by other agencies) and may request separate funds to raise salaries for hard-to-fill positions. They DO NOT decide federal employee wages.

Federal employees wages are decided by a wage scale authorized and set by congress.

see:

Treasury, Postal Service and General Government Appropriations Act, 1991
H.R.2029 - Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2016

and the like. Note that congressmen who lower federal employee wages without touching their own will give political opponents a good talking point.

If Trump wants to freeze recruitment he can do so by appointing an OPM director who will simply refuse to hire. This would be a very bad decision (practically, not politically) if implemented across the board. For all the fat that needs to be trimmed there are a few places new employees are desperately needed.

If he wants to reduce federal employee wages he need the support of Congress.
